details: CONFIRMED by reading. rules/structured-data.md: "No new label or regex search over markdown to get a value out of
it. A reviewer flags one, and the fix is to store that value as data." rules/taste.md:10-11 makes `why` starting with
`taste: <change>` the value the 5-change count reads. The brief asked for the marker in found_in and to report if
`relay queue add` cannot set it; the worker reported it and moved the marker into prose. found_in is an existing
schema field (FIELD_ORDER, STRINGS) and add(context=...) already writes it, so the fix is not a new store.
Inside: the change's promise (countable kept vs dropped) needs this file. Rule label: Structured data.
Size: 15 agent minutes (key, mapping to context, 2 tests, rule text and its pinned test phrase).
evidence: lib/relay_queue.py:597  def add(..., context="relay queue add", ...)  -> new_item(..., found_in=context, ...)
rules/taste.md:10  fix item whose `why` starts with `taste: <change>` (`relay queue add` always writes its own `found_in`).
failing_case: The front queues a taste item as the rule says: input why = "taste: core-tests-not-in-gate\nchecker ran twice".
Counting = items whose why[0] starts with "taste:". An item written "Taste: ..." or "waste (taste: x)" or one whose
why is later re-worded is silently not counted, and the measurement is a label search over prose.
Trying the structured way today: an input with found_in = "taste: core-tests-not-in-gate" is refused by
read_add_input (unknown key: ADD_KEYS lacks found_in), although add() already takes `context` and writes it as found_in.
Should: `relay queue add --input` accept found_in, and the rule count items by the found_in field.
fix_hint: Add "found_in" to ADD_KEYS; in read_add_input treat it like title/where (a text) and store it as out["context"];
bin/relay already passes **fields to add(). Change rules/taste.md lines 9-11 to found_in = "taste: <change>" and the
count to found_in; update the phrase in TestTasteRule.

pass_cases: 1. relay queue add --input with title, why, time, failing_case and found_in = "taste: demo" -> the item JSON has found_in "taste: demo"; why is stored as given.
2. relay queue add --input without found_in -> found_in "relay queue add" (as today).
3. relay queue add --from review.json F7 -> found_in "finding F7 of review.json" (as today, tests/test_queue.py:176).
4. found_in given as a list or a number -> refused, naming `found_in`.
5. rules/taste.md says the marker is found_in = "taste: <change>" and the count is items whose found_in starts with "taste: " (kept = state not dropped).
reason: Owner's word recorded on F1: counting and marker removed; rules/taste.md has no marker or count, and relay_queue.py equals master. Moot.
findings.summary: Structured data: the taste count reads a `taste:` label out of the free-text `why` instead of the `found_in` field

details: Question for the owner. How it works: the judge base says a project rule that raises a finding sets its severity;
this rule raises waste flags but sets none. Live example: in this review F4 is a waste flag rated LOW (correct today,
cheap), F2 MEDIUM because it also breaks the "relay only" decision. Answers:
(a, recommended) waste alone is LOW: listed, fixed when cheap, else queued with the taste marker; it never holds a merge
during the experiment. (b) waste is MEDIUM: fixed before the merge, which lengthens every change during the trial.
Size: 5 agent minutes once decided.
failing_case: A reviewer finds "the checker is run twice by the new flow". Under the judge base, MEDIUM is fixed before merge
with no deferral; LOW is fixed when cheap, else listed and dropped. rules/taste.md:8 says only "lists the waste".
Two reviewers may rate the same flag MEDIUM (merge waits) and LOW (dropped), and "flags the owner keeps" mixes both.
fix_hint: One sentence in rules/taste.md: "A reviewer's waste flag is LOW unless it also breaks another rule; one not fixed in the change is queued with the taste marker."
pass_cases: 1. rules/taste.md states the severity (or the rule for choosing it) of a waste flag found before the merge.
2. rules/taste.md states whether such a flag blocks the merge or is queued.
reason: rules/taste.md: "waste that repeats on every run or every change is MEDIUM and is fixed before the merge; a one-off is LOW."
findings.summary: the rule sets no severity for a reviewer's waste flag, so whether it blocks the merge is left to each reviewer
